title: Human_Problem_Solving
summary:
Human Problem Solving (1972) is a book by Allen Newell and Herbert A. Simon. First published in 1972, this monumental work develops and defends the authors' information processing theory of human reasoning. Human reasoners, they argue, can be modeled as symbolic information processing systems (IPSs), abstracted entirely from physiological bases.

The authors first develop the formal theory of information processing systems. They then report studies of three symbolic reasoning tasks and analyze the data using the information processing paradigm. In the final section, they state their comprehensive theory of human problem-solving. Newell and Simon argue that human thinking is an information processing system, just as a computer is. Problem solving is essentially a search through an abstract problem space, navigated using operators that transform the current information state into a new one.

The success of the models of cognition given in this work was a major piece of evidence for the physical symbol system hypothesis, which Newell and Simon would first state a few years later. Newell went on to co-develop the Soar cognitive architecture, and Simon received the Nobel Prize in Economics. The two jointly received the Turing Award in 1975 for the research program of which Human Problem Solving was the culmination.

Their previous epoch-making collaborations included the General Problem Solver, the Logic Theorist, and the Information Processing Language. This book represents a careful application of ideas from artificial intelligence to cognitive psychology, drawn from AI's first golden age.
